correctness.rationale: Each aaa forces aa into the code; those diagonal pairs also cover all words with repeated letters. Taking the complement on off-diagonal ordered pairs converts every remaining forbidden uncovered word abc into the non-induced transitive triangle a→b, a→c, b→c, with opposite arcs allowed. In a feasible digraph, endpoints of any arc have disjoint out-neighborhoods and disjoint in-neighborhoods. Summing the degree bounds on arcs gives Σ_v d(v)^2≤2qE; Cauchy–Schwarz gives 4E²/q≤Σ_v d(v)^2. The bidirected balanced bipartite construction attains floor(q²/2) arcs. At even q, equality packs the out-neighborhoods across each arc into all q vertices, forcing the reverse arc, after which Mantel equality gives the balanced bipartition. At odd q=2m+1, an extremizer has some vertex of total degree at most 2m; removing it and applying the even bound forces degree exactly 2m and an even extremizer on the other vertices. Each of the deleted vertex's in- and out-neighborhoods must be one whole side of that K_{m,m}, as both are independent and their sizes sum to 2m. They must be the same side, since different sides yield a transitive triangle through the deleted vertex. This establishes exactly the stated codebooks including q=2 and q=3. The labeled count follows by choosing the smaller part, or halving for equal parts; all are conjugate under relabeling. Independently, `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_math_replay.py 2` used direct set-cover recursion on ordered distinct-letter words for q=2..5; it returned (size, count)=(2,1),(5,3),(8,3),(13,10) and found only the asserted partitions. This finite check is not the all-q argument.

originality.rationale: The finite directed Turán classification already gives the full codebook rigidity, not just the scalar bound. Lemma 4.1 of Kühn–Osthus–Townsend–Zhao applies exactly to the complement model at (k,n,a)=(2,q,2) and proves uniqueness of the bidirected balanced bipartition. The labeled count then follows by counting the placements of that unique extremizer. Their proof explicitly credits the a=2 case to Brown–Harary (1970).

value.rationale: Classifying arbitrary optimizers rather than just giving their cardinality is a natural question. Here, however, the claimed classification is a direct transfer of an existing exact extremal theorem; its label count and one-orbit assertion are simple consequences. The elementary proof is useful exposition but the record does not establish an additional nonmechanical scientific claim.
